title: Revealing the bacterial butyrate synthesis pathways by analyzing (meta)genomic data
authors: Vital M, Howe AC, Tiedje JM
population: 3,184 sequenced bacterial genomes and 15 stool metagenomes of healthy individuals from the Human Microbiome Project
funder: Financial support was provided by the NIH Human Microbiome Project Demonstration Project (UH3 DK083993).
result: 225 genomes carried a butyrate synthesis pathway. Four pathways (acetyl-CoA, glutarate, 4-aminobutyrate, lysine) converge on the conversion of crotonyl-CoA to butyryl-CoA by the butyryl-CoA dehydrogenase–electron-transferring flavoprotein complex, a step postulated to conserve energy through ferredoxin reduction. In the acetyl-CoA pathway, thiolase, β-hydroxybutyryl-CoA dehydrogenase and crotonase precede this step, and butyryl-CoA:acetate CoA-transferase or phosphate butyryltransferase with butyrate kinase forms butyrate. In stool metagenomes the acetyl-CoA pathway made up a mean 79.7% of butyrate pathways; for that pathway the terminal genes but and buk had median abundances of 77.2% and 21.8%. Butyrate is described as the main energy source for colonocytes.
